concept.title: A worked case: two calendars in one life
concept.shortdesc: How far apart the Julian and Gregorian calendars were in the life of a diarist who lived from 1671 to 1704.

conbody.p: Abraham De la Pryme was a diarist in Yorkshire. England used the Julian calendar all through his life, so his dates are Julian. This case shows how far they were from the Gregorian calendar. Read first.

section.title: Ten days, and then eleven
section.p: The Gregorian calendar was ten days ahead when Abraham was born. The gap grew while he lived. The year 1700 had a 29 February in the Julian calendar, but not in the Gregorian calendar. So, from March 1700, the gap was eleven days.

table.title: Four of his dates in both calendars

section.p: uFTi does not work out the other calendar for you. We worked out this table by hand.

section.title: A day of the week can show the calendar
section.p: A friend wrote in his own diary that Abraham died on a Monday, the 12th of the month. The preface of the printed diary gives this, for June 1704. In the Julian calendar, 12 June 1704 was a Monday. In the Gregorian calendar, it was a Thursday. So the friend's date is a Julian one.
When a record names the day of the week, you can test its date in this way.

section.title: What his dates cannot show
section.p: Abraham died in 1704, so his dates stop before the change of 1752. explains that change.

section.title: What to record
section.p: Keep the date as the record gives it. If you want to show which calendar it is, type its name first, such as Julian 12 June 1704.
